title: How Dementia Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain dementia as a set of symptoms rather than a single disease, distinguishing it from normal age-related forgetfulness and mild cognitive impairment. They cover the main causes and types: Alzheimer's (amyloid plaques and tau tangles), vascular dementia (strokes), Lewy body dementia (linked to Robin Williams and Parkinson's), frontotemporal dementia (formerly Pick's disease), Huntington's, prion diseases, and reversible dementia. They discuss diagnosis tests (MMSE and the clock drawing test), complications such as medication management, nutrition, hygiene and depression, caregiver burden, treatments (cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, blood thinners, antipsychotics), preventive habits, the Dementia Friendly America initiative, and the Dutch dementia village. The episode ends with listener mail about Hecky Krasnow, who produced songs for Captain Kangaroo.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to dementia
segments.summary: Hosts banter about the 'Stint of Noel' name, then Chuck and Josh introduce dementia as a set of symptoms rather than a disease, distinguishing it from normal age-related forgetfulness.

segments.title: Prevalence and cost of dementia
segments.summary: Discussion of how many Americans have dementia, projected growth as baby boomers age, and the projected health care costs.

segments.title: Diagnostic criteria for dementia
segments.summary: Dementia is diagnosed as memory loss plus at least one of aphasia, apraxia, agnosia, or executive dysfunction. The hosts note that dementia is a symptom set brought on by disease.

segments.title: Alzheimer's disease as a cause of dementia
segments.summary: Alzheimer's is the most common cause of dementia, linked to amyloid plaques and tau tangles that kill neurons. Genetic risk factors include the APOE gene, family history, and Down syndrome. The disease typically lasts three to five years after diagnosis, though it can last up to a decade.

segments.title: Vascular dementia and strokes
segments.summary: Vascular dementia, accounting for about 20 percent of cases, results from strokes, either one large event or many small ones. Josh describes his grandfather's stroke and resulting loss of speech.

segments.title: Lewy body dementia and Parkinson's
segments.summary: Lewy body dementia, around 5 percent of cases, causes intense visual hallucinations and Parkinson's-like symptoms. The hosts mention Robin Williams had it at autopsy, and discuss Parkinson's and the film Awakenings.

segments.title: Frontotemporal dementia and Huntington's disease
segments.summary: Frontotemporal dementia (formerly Pick's disease) affects personality, behavior and language and often strikes people between 40 and 70, with risky behavior and blunted emotions. Huntington's causes uncontrolled movements and can be inherited.

segments.title: Prion disease, TBI, and reversible dementia
segments.summary: Other causes include prion diseases like Creutzfeldt-Jakob, which is rare and linked to infected tissue, and dementia from head trauma or concussions in athletes. Some dementia from vitamin deficiency or medications is reversible, while age-associated dementia is not. Mild cognitive impairment is the intermediate stage, and early diagnosis matters.

segments.title: Diagnosing dementia: MMSE and clock drawing test
segments.summary: Doctors assess the patient's history and the Mini Mental State Examination, plus the clock drawing test, which checks verbal understanding, memory, spatial knowledge and constructive skills. The clock test was developed in the sixties and gained use in the eighties.

segments.title: Dementia complications, caregiving and society
segments.summary: Complications include forgetting medications, nutrition and swallowing problems, poor hygiene, depression and agitation, and safety risks. The Dementia Friendly America initiative trains service workers. Caregiver burden is discussed, along with the Dutch dementia village and treatments such as cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, blood thinners, and antipsychotics. Preventive habits like puzzles and moderate drinking are mentioned.

segments.title: Closing thoughts and listener mail on Hecky Krasnow
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on their own dementia risk, then read listener mail from Aiden in Maryland about his great-grandfather Hecky Krasnow, who produced songs for Captain Kangaroo, and suggest a possible episode.
